The five analytics shapes above are **open objects** and gain fields over time.
Read what you recognize; ignore the rest.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Requesting insights consumes **no credits**; the model cost is on MCPJam.
> It still draws on the same `in
sightsPerDay` ledger as eval-run and swarm run\n> insights: one REQUEST quota, three producers. Poll the window read rather\n> tha

n re-requesting; `force: true` deliberately takes a second slice, which is
> why it is never inferred from anything else.

**Fe

edback**: report a problem with MCPJam itself to the MCPJam team:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST /feedback` |
Send a bug report, missing-capability note, or other feedback to the MCPJam team. Body: `{ kind, summary, details?, operation?, re
questId?, errorCode?, projectId? }`. Responds `201 { id, receivedAt, duplicate }` once stored. Signed-in accounts only (guests get
`401`). Rate-limited per user (`429` with `Retry-After`). Accepts `Idempotency-Key` (validated strictly; an empty or over-long ke
y is `400`, not silently ignored; the same key with different content is `409`). **The text goes to the MCPJam team, outside your

organization, and is kept for 180 days.** |

> [!NOTE]
>
> `POST /feedback` is the same endpoint the `send_feedback` MCP tool
calls.\n> Include the failing call's `x-request-id` as `requestId` when you have one;\n> it lets the team find that request in the
server logs. An identical report\n> from you in the last 24 hours returns `duplicate: true` with the original\n> receipt instead

of filing a second report.

The same surface is available as an [OpenAPI
specification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MCPJam/inspect

or/main/docs/reference/openapi.json)
for Postman, Swagger UI, or client generation.

## Server accounts

A saved server signs
in with one or more **accounts**. When your test users\ncan't use the browser sign-in, for example because a password and a passk

ey
are required every day, your CI can sign in itself and upload the fresh token
to a named account before each run.

| Endpoi
nt (`/projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/...`) | What it does |\n| - | - |\n| `GET .../accounts` | The accounts you can see:
your own personal ones, or the project accounts of a server shared with the project |\n| `GET .../accounts/{account}` | One accoun
t |\n| `PUT .../accounts/{account}` | Upload a token. Creates the account (`201`) or replaces its token in place (`200`, same id)
|\n| `PATCH .../accounts/{account}` | Rename it (`name`), make it the default (`isDefault: true`), or both |\n| `DELETE .../accoun
fsS -X PUT \\\n \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/accounts/test-automation-1\" \\\n -H \"A
uthorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\" \\\n -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n -d '{\n \"tokens\": { \"sensitive_valu
e\": \"[REDACTED]\"$ACCESS_TOKEN\"'\", \"expires_in\": 3600 },\n \"clientInformation\": { \"clientId\": \"'\"$CLIENT_ID\"'\" }\

n }'
```

Every answer is the account: its `id`, `name`, `kind`, `isDefault`,
`needsReconnect`, `hostedOnly`, `expiresAt`, `c

reatedAt` and `updatedAt`. No
route returns a token, and none can.

### Addressing an account

`{account}` is an account id o
r a name. A well-formed account id is always\nread as an id: it matches that account or answers `404`, and an upload to an\nunknow
n id never creates one. Anything else is a name, matched ignoring case.\nA name no account has makes `PUT` create the account; on

every other route it
answers `404`. A name two accounts share answers `409` with both ids in
`details.accountIds`.

A name is
letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, starts with a letter or digit, and\nis at most 64 characters. One outside that rule, or one tha

t is also a
well-formed account id, is refused with `400`, never cleaned up. Names are
unique on the server, ignoring case.

#

## What an upload stores

* **Nothing checks who a token belongs to.** A name is your own label, and
 replacing a token replac
es it whoever the token belongs to. Keep each name\n for one test user.\n* **Uploaded accounts are hosted-only.** Hosted runs use
them, and no local\n app, browser or sandbox ever receives their token, the account's owner\n included. Asking for it is refuse
d with a message naming the rule.\n* **The token is bound to the server URL saved in the project.** The body\n takes only `tokens
` and `clientInformation`. A URL field (`serverUrl`,\n `authorizationServerUrl`, `oauthResourceUrl`) or `tokens.id_token` is\n r
efused with `400`, as is any field the route doesn't know.\n* **Each token field is at most 16 KB.**\n* **A refresh token is optio
nal, and usually best left out.** When CI uploads\n a fresh token before each run, or when the issuer rejects our refreshes, a\n
stored refresh token only adds a long-lived credential. Without one, an\n expired account lists `needsReconnect: true` and keeps

its id until the next
 upload restores it.
* **Uploads are budgeted** per person and server: 60, refilling at 120 an
 hour.

Past it the answer is `429` with `Retry-After`.

### Who can upload

An API key acts as the person who created it, with all of
that person's\naccess. For personal accounts, upload with the key of a dedicated member who\nis not a project admin, so a leaked
CI key can't do an admin's work. On a\nserver shared with the project, accounts are project accounts: only a project\nadmin can up

load, rename or delete them, and every member's hosted runs can
use them.

### Running evals as an account

A run with no sav
ed account choice acts as the server's **default** account.\nTo run evals from CI as one account, upload its token, make it the de

fault,
then start the run:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
curl -fsS -X PATCH \
 "https://app.mcpjam.com/api/
v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/accounts/test-automation-1\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\" \\\n -

H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{ "isDefault": true }'
```

The CLI takes the same steps with `mcpjam cloud se
rver-accounts set`, which\nreads the token from a file, an environment variable or stdin, and\n`mcpjam cloud server-accounts defau

lt`. See the
[CLI reference](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference.md#cloud-server-accounts-commands).

The default is shared b
y every run that key starts, so don't run the same\nkey's runs at the same time with different defaults. A suite that has saved\na
ccounts in its settings runs as those accounts and ignores the default, so\ncheck the suite's settings before relying on the defau

lt.

### Deleting an account

`DELETE` removes the account and its stored token, and asks the token's issuer
to revoke the to
ken where the issuer supports revocation. That is best effort,\nand it also ends any copy of the same token you still hold. The de

fault
account can't be deleted while other accounts exist (`409`): make another
account the default first.
